title: Host Access Token claim set
description: Claims of the short-lived JWT a host issues so that a plugin can read one invocation's payload from the host API in pull mode. It is deliberately a SEPARATE token type from any token a host issues to a user or to a browser: RFC 8725 warns that the cheapest way to break a JWT deployment is to let one verifier accept a token minted for something else, so this token carries its own `typ` header (`ct-host-access+jwt`), its own signing key, its own issuer/audience pair, and a `scope` with exactly one value. A verifier MUST pin all of them; accepting this token anywhere other than the payload endpoint is a defect, not a convenience. The token binds the read to a single invocation AND to the deployment that was current when the invocation was created, so a token cannot be replayed across a plugin upgrade or rollback. It carries no personal data: no name, no phone number, no tree content - only opaque identifiers - because a bearer credential ends up in more logs than any payload does. Presenting it is necessary but never sufficient: the pull request must also carry the direction-scoped HMAC signature described in docs/security.md.

iss.description: Fixed issuer. A verifier pins this exact value rather than accepting any issuer it happens to have a key for.

aud.description: Exactly two audience values: the fixed logical audience 'contenttree-plugin-host' and the normalized origin of the host API this token may be presented to (RFC 8707 resource binding). Binding the concrete origin means a token minted for one deployment of the host cannot be replayed against another.

sub.description: The plugin the token was issued to, in the form 'plugin:{plugin_id}'. The prefix keeps this subject namespace disjoint from any user subject namespace, so a user-token verifier can never be tricked into treating a plugin as a user.
sub.$comment: The trailing negative lookahead is an ECMA-262-compatible exact end-of-input assertion.

jti.description: Unique identifier for this token. It is independent of any user-token identifier so that replay bookkeeping for the two token types cannot collide.

invocation_id.description: The single invocation whose payload this token may read.

revision_id.description: Optional immutable revision the invocation was pinned to.
revision_id.$comment: The trailing negative lookahead is an ECMA-262-compatible exact end-of-input assertion.

deployment_id.description: The deployment the invocation was pinned to. Required: it is what makes the token useless after an upgrade or rollback replaces the running instance.
deployment_id.$comment: The trailing negative lookahead is an ECMA-262-compatible exact end-of-input assertion.

scope.description: Exactly one scope, expressed as a fixed string rather than a list, so there is no room for a token that reads a payload and also does something else.

exp.description: Expiry. The lifetime is short (10 minutes is the documented default) and a verifier tolerates at most 60 seconds of clock skew.
